sources.title: INAH: Cantona archaeological site
sources.note: Direct site inventory: residential compounds, Patio 2 and Calzada 1. Public map audit independently verified in local decoded snapshots; exact-site occupation is not inferred from continued shading.

sources.title: INAH: Museo de Sitio de Cantona
sources.note: Direct excavation-based museum inventory, food vessels, grinding stones and ixtle tools. Site-wide assemblages are not assigned invented exact years or a single household.

sources.title: Ángel García-Cook and D. Tenorio (2010): Estudio de procedencia de obsidiana arqueológica de Cantona, Puebla
sources.note: Full indexed original abstract of Arqueología 43, 217 to 229. Direct fetch failed. 79 samples and neutron activation; Oyameles-Zaragoza source result distinguished from sampling of other local materials.

sources.title: Edgar Tavares López: Ciudad prehispánica de Cantona, Hereditas (2004)
sources.note: Direct PDF, printed pages 18 to 19 (human PDF pages 18 to 19). Tour with excavation director Ángel García Cook: peak 600 to 900, abandonment 900 to 1050. Claims restricted to article, not entire magazine.

sources.title: INAH: Xochicalco archaeological site
sources.note: Direct named-structure descriptions: cistern, steam bath, builders tools and two-glyph stela. Epiclassic 650 to 900 site context. Scientific precision of proposed calendar adjustment, ethnic identifications and superlatives not adopted.

sources.title: Silvia Garza Tarazona: Lápida de Xochicalco, un ejemplo de escritura mesoamericana
sources.note: Direct scholarly museum interpretation of object 10-344139, from Xochicalco; broad Classic date 200 to 900 CE. Proposed marriage reading and tentative toponyms explicitly qualified. Obsolete blanket classification as semi-writing not adopted.

sources.title: Geoffrey McCafferty (2008): Cholula culture history
sources.note: Direct researcher account: Early Postclassic UA-1 spinning/waterfowl, early polychrome pottery, cultural change and approximate 1200 political transition. Group author website pages as one work conservatively.

sources.title: Bryan Cockrell (2017), Metropolitan Museum of Art: Bell, 1987.394.624
sources.note: Direct metadata and full indexed original curatorial essay. Broad eleventh to sixteenth century date, West Mexico or Valley of Mexico, copper or alloy; no exact excavation provenance. Alloy composition inferred from parallels; do not claim object tested.

sources.title: INAH: Yagul, Palacio de los Seis Patios
sources.note: Direct palace description; Late Postclassic 1200 to 1521, public/private court interpretations and possibly ruler-family central courts. Group with existing official 08_yagul.pdf guide attribution.

sources.title: INALI: Atlas de las Lenguas Indígenas de México
sources.note: Institutional description of current Indigenous language communities. Used for living diversity, not projecting present classifications or numbers onto 800 CE.

batchIdentityNotes.scope: Exact missing HB cultural record, 800 to 1279 CE. No aliases. This geometry is primarily western/central Mexico, Gulf Coast and Oaxaca, not the whole Mesoamerican culture area. Maya, Nahua, Zapotec, Mixtec and named-state dossiers remain separate.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded world-800, world-1000 and world-1200 point checks: Cantona, El Tajin, Yagul, Mitla inside; Tula and Cacaxtla outside; Xochicalco inside 800 only; Cholula inside 1000 and 1200 but outside 800. Chichen Itza outside throughout. Public wording reflects coarse changes without claims of annexation.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Regional phases, not succession of rulers. Cantona peak 600 to 900 and abandonment 900 to 1050 predate end; Cholula Early Postclassic persists. Yagul 1200 to 1521 and bell eleventh to sixteenth centuries explicitly mostly beyond span; Xochicalco slab 200 to 900 may predate the opening.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Authentic modern sign reading Year 10 Reed / day 9 Reptile Eye from Xochicalco stela. No invented ancient-language wording or Unicode glyph reconstruction. English names translate INAH Spanish sign readings. Original in museum, replica on plaza; no Gregorian date conversion. Marriage-slab narrative separately tentative.
batchIdentityNotes.evidenceLimits: No unsupported school, medical efficacy or universal household plumbing/toilets. Steam bath is a specific ritual installation. Feather textile use, palace-family room use and marriage alliance are interpretations. Source-date and cultural classifications do not establish exact ethnic identities for anonymous inhabitants.
